Lung cancer is the most frequently occurring cancer and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide . Pulmonary resection is key treatment for lung cancer but is often accompanied by significant postoperative complications, which may prolong hospital stay and incur greater medical expenses [1]. Surgical approaches for lung cancer, including video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and thoracotomy, offer distinct advantages and challenges. Previous studies [2, 3] suggest that VATS is superior to thoracotomy due to fewer postoperative complications.
